title: [finding] DELETE on a package-declared `sys_permission_set` answers `200 {success:true}` and changes nothing — byte-identical envelope to a real delete, so a UI fires a success toast and the row comes back on refresh
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` seat 3 (`session_01HnRAeVTLJevtQ5iCPX6JSm`) out of the #19195 reading round. ⛔ Not triaged, ⛔ no `domain:*`, ⛔ no priority — routing and first-touch grading are the triage seat's sole production. The fix lands in `packages/plugins/plugin-security`, which the domain table assigns to `domain:services`.

⏱️ Measured 2026-09-20T10:27–10:36Z against `origin/main` `f93beea0a69ba0780347d16e883cc47ef4ab57b1`, on `examples/app-showcase` booted fresh, seeded platform admin `admin@objectos.ai` over a cookie session — i.e. an ordinary **non-system** REST caller. Reproduced twice.

## The defect

`DELETE /api/v1/data/sys_permission_set/{id}` on a **package-declared** set answers:

```
200 {"object":"sys_permission_set","id":"...","success":true}
```

…and **changes nothing**: the row is still present, with the **same id** (so it was not deleted-and-recreated) and an **unchanged `updated_at`**.

The identical call on an **environment-authored** set really deletes it (row count 18 → 17).

⇒ Both outcomes ship a **byte-identical envelope**. Nothing in the status, the body or a header distinguishes 「I deleted it」 from 「I silently did nothing」. A UI fires a success toast and shows the row again on refresh.

## ⭐ The same product already ships the discriminator, on the sibling door

`DELETE /api/v1/meta/permission/showcase_auditor` answers:

```json
{"success":true,"reset":false,"message":"No customization overlay found ... already at artifact default."}
```

⇒ the metadata door carries `reset: false` for exactly this intent. The data door drops it. So this is not 「a discriminator would have to be invented」 — it is one door not carrying what its sibling already declares.

## Why this is a defect and not a preference

This is the shape 「machine-readable surfaces must not lie」 exists to catch (AGENTS.md, Route and surface ownership rule 4), and the ADR-0049 class more broadly: a declared outcome (`success: true`) that the runtime does not honour. ⛔ A caller cannot act differently on the two cases, which is the branch-information test the spec lane charter names.

## Controls, so no reading here is a dead query

`POST` of a new set → **201**; `PATCH` of that set → **200**; `DELETE` of that set → **200** and the row really went (18 → 17). ⇒ the door accepts writes and `DELETE` is **not** a universal no-op. Unauthenticated `PATCH` on the same URL → **401** `UNAUTHENTICATED`, proving the `code` field discriminates rather than being constant.

⚠️ Every HTTP status was captured with `curl -w` **before any pipe**; no `head -N` sat upstream of a status read.

## Dedupe words

`sys_permission_set delete no-op` · `packaged permission set DELETE success true` · `data door delete reset discriminator` · `ADR-0094 delete reset not refused` · `permission set delete 200 unchanged`

Origin: #19195 (the reading request), comment `5749267535` carries the full cross-tab.
